segmentation.text: must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. No named class stands in for it.

DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'. st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; st.median_or_divider: 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'; st.on_way ties the divider to the highway h; rel.occupies anchors the subject on h. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's motion.

'any left turn' is drv.motion.left_turn, 'Road user a has completed a turn to the left', a heading change to the left between turn_min and u_turn_min; 'U-turn' (DEF-NRS-484B-077, 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction') is drv.motion.u_turn, whose contract quotes that definition; a 'semicircular turn' is a turn through half a circle, a reversal of direction, which drv.motion.u_turn's band denotes. Both concepts read kin.yaw_rate through prim.heading_change and say nothing of the place, which the trigger and exceptions supply.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': a turn 'through an opening' is one whose path overlaps (rel.occupies) a divider region of h that carries the opening attribute.

A crossover is a divider region with the opening attribute; an intersection is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; a turn 'at' it is one whose path overlaps it (rel.occupies). 'Established by a public authority' is a legal status read through the feature's presence.

applicability: At an observation at which drv.motion.left_turn(subject) or drv.motion.u_turn(subject) holds (the turn recognized; each holds at its recognition only), with window p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min and yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol, where at some observation of the window behind it of length p.vehicle_turn_window (the turn under way) the subject occupied a highway h on which a median_or_divider region lies (st.on_way).
obligation: The turn is made through an opening, a crossover or an intersection: at some observation of that same window the subject's footprint overlapped a median_or_divider region lying on h that carries the opening attribute, or an intersection lying on h. Where it overlapped none of them at any observation of the window, the turn violates the duty; where an overlap is unobserved and none is observed, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'semicircular turn' is read as a reversal of direction, the band of drv.motion.u_turn; a semicircle that does not reverse the heading is no semicircular turn.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's motion on the highway, whoever or whatever controls it.
'established by a public authority' is a legal status; the crossover or intersection present on the road is its evidence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On highway h with a st.median_or_divider without opening, the subject makes a reversal of direction (drv.motion.u_turn rises) whose path crosses the divider away from any intersection and any region with the opening attribute.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On h the subject makes a U-turn whose path overlaps a divider region carrying the opening attribute (a crossover).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject makes a left turn on a highway on which no st.median_or_divider lies.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject on divided highway h reverses direction across the divider; kin.yaw_rate is absent, so neither left_turn nor u_turn can be recognized.

scenarios.name: occasion_b
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies divided highway h during the first part of its left turn's window; the turn carries it across h's divider, where it has no opening, into a driveway beyond h: the trigger held for part of the turn and no opening or intersection was overlapped.

scenarios.name: occasion_b_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject left divided highway h before its turn window began and makes a U-turn on an undivided highway: the trigger held only before the turn.

scenarios.name: occasion_f
scenarios.narrative: The subject's U-turn on h overlaps a divider region carrying the opening attribute during part of its window.

scenarios.name: occasion_f_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject overlapped a divider opening on h only before its turn window began; the U-turn itself crosses the divider where it has no opening and overlaps no intersection.

scenarios.name: occasion_g
scenarios.narrative: The subject's left turn on h overlaps an intersection lying on h during part of its window.

scenarios.name: occasion_g_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupied an intersection on h only before its turn window began; it then makes a U-turn across the divider mid-block, overlapping no opening and no intersection.

under_way.words: its heading change over the window behind the observation
under_way.justification: The turn is under way within the window behind its recognition, over which prim.heading_change integrates kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'): the road user's motion, not the region it occupies, tells the turn from what came before.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: turning-movement durations at urban junctions in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading changes of a few degrees versus junction turns of about ninety degrees in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: midpoint between a right-angle turn and a full reversal of direction

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of vehicle inertial measurement
